topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture themes and outlines the expected learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the study of tumor viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and experimental assays for cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the classifications of cancer-associated genes and illustrate how mutation types, allele dosage, and pathway controls govern their functions.

topics.label: Mechanisms and types of genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer, detailing how specific defects in DNA repair pathways, replication, and mitosis generate genomic abnormalities.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives cancer progression and shapes tumor evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the lecture, invites questions, and provides recommended reading.
